newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.11 pct in July.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Fipe inflation 0.11 pct in July.

text.p: Brazil's inflation as measured by the Economic Research Institute (Fipe) fell to 0.11 percent in July compared with a 1.42 percent rise in consumer prices in June, a Fipe official said.

Fipe chief Juarez Rizzieri said a drop in clothing and food prices last month and stabilising public service rates were behind the drop in the Fipe index, which measures inflation in the Sao Paulo area.
Rizzieri also said personal expenses and education costs declined in July, while housing, transportation and health service prices rose.
He forecast inflation in August between zero and 0.5 percent as clothing and food prices continue to decline.
With last month's figure, inflation reached 4.24 percent for the first seven months of the year and 5.81 percent in the 12-month period ended July 31, according to Fipe.
Rizzieri released the following breakdown of Fipe's weighted inflation index for July:
- Food: -0.28 pct drop in the month
- Housing: 0.75 pct rise in the month
- Transportation: 1.20 pct rise in the month
- Personal Expenses: -0.13 pct drop in the month
- Clothing: -1.75 pct drop in the month
- Health care: 0.50 pct rise in the month
- Education: -0.13 pct rise in the month
The Fipe index is calculated by the University of Sao Paulo, which releases inflation figures weekly.
